text: This is a real Pi terminal recording with sf-pi and Jev. The eight log files are generated test data.
All 23 sf-pi extensions have loaded. The startup catalog has 43 registered tools; the normal active tools remain available.
Enable exact excerpts with /jev-context excerpts. Jev now shows its status above the prompt. The target is 50% fewer serialized request bytes.
Pi is asked to read eight full logs, in order, and report the latest owner, build, region, and rollout state.
Early checks keep the originals: the first has no completed tool text; the next two cannot reach 50% because instructions and tool schemas remain protected.
Jev starts applying exact excerpts. The first applied request is 57.1% smaller in bytes; later reductions vary. Full originals remain retained.
Later requests also pass the 50% byte check. Only completed tool text is reduced; instructions and tool definitions remain protected.
Pi asks jev_context_read for omitted detail. It retrieves the last log in four pages before giving its answer.
The final answer matches the fixture: Mira, build-642, us-west, paused. This answer used excerpts plus retrieval of original text.
/jev-context log shows every check and application, the request byte reduction, tool-text sizes, and clearly labeled token estimates.
Now test one specific retained line. Pi is asked to retrieve line 420 of log-08.txt with jev_context_read, without reading the filesystem.
The tool retrieves the original line using its host-issued reference. The returned source hash matches the original file.
Recovered exactly: ORION-7E4C-RECOVERED. Keeping original text makes omitted details available after compression.
The activity log records both turns. All 15 gateway responses returned HTTP 200; all tool calls succeeded in this bounded test.
Pi exits normally. This demonstrates visible checks, validated request byte reduction, and original-text retrieval. Token, cost, and production quality gains need separate measurement.
